name: Consensus
description: An experimental neural-feed film designed for exactly two simultaneous viewers whose BCIs are networked together — you experience the narrative as yourself, but with the constant awareness of the other person's emotional state running beneath your own like a second heartbeat, and the film's plot (a couple negotiating a contract that will separate them permanently) only resolves differently depending on what each viewer actually feels rather than what the characters say. No two pairs have ever reported the same ending. Created by the artist collective Residue, it was distributed exclusively as paired sessions at unlicensed feed-parlors.
cultural_impact: Sparked a genuine philosophical debate in GLMZ about whether neural-feed intimacy constitutes a new category of relationship, and the term 'running Consensus' became slang for any partnership where both parties are uncomfortably aware of what the other actually wants.
story_hooks: Someone is running an unauthorized version of Consensus without telling one of the two viewers that they're networked — using it to extract genuine emotional intelligence from targets for corporate espionage.

A pair of Residue collective members who created the film ran it themselves and haven't been able to fully separate since; one of them wants help finding a way to sever the connection before it destroys both of them.

A Spire family is willing to pay enormously to acquire the Consensus architecture for private use — and the players need to decide whether to sell it, destroy it, or find out what a Spire family wants with a device that makes you feel what someone else truly feels.
